sc: Large plethoric baby, jittery at 2 hours, low glucose → IDM hypoglycaemia (hyperinsulinism)
Home birth, no vitamin K, breastfed, melaena on day 3, PT long, platelets normal → Vitamin K deficiency bleeding
Hypocalcaemia with cleft palate and heart defect → DiGeorge syndrome
f: Macrosomia, shoulder dystocia · hypoglycaemia, hypocalcaemia · RDS · polycythaemia · HCM (thick septum) · caudal regression (most specific)
Treat if < 2.6 mmol/L · well baby: feed + dextrose gel 0.5 ml/kg · symptomatic: 10% glucose 2 ml/kg IV then infusion
Total Ca < 2 mmol/L · jittery, tetany, seizures · 10% calcium gluconate 2 ml/kg slow IV · not responding → magnesium
Haematocrit > 65% · SGA, IDM, delayed clamping · plethora, lethargy, hypoglycaemia · symptomatic: partial exchange with saline
Early (maternal drugs) · classic day 2–7 · late (breastfed, cholestasis) · vitamin K 1 mg IV + FFP 10–15 ml/kg if severe
Physiological anaemia lowest at 8–12 weeks · glucose infusion > 8 mg/kg/min = hyperinsulinism (diazoxide)
trap: Jittery newborn: glucose first, then calcium · vomited blood with adult Hb on Apt test = swallowed maternal blood · factors II, VII, IX, X are vitamin K-dependent
